title: Streamflow segmentation telemetry: per-segment metrics, span linking, and redaction
creator: Maya Lin
description:
Goal: implement a robust, low-overhead observability layer for streaming responses that (1) emits per-segment metrics for every logical stream slice, (2) correlates each segment with trace spans and request provenance, and (3) redacts sensitive content in logs/metrics in real time. This ticket covers the runtime instrumentation, SDK compatibility layer for older clients, and integration points with function/tool-calling and structured-output modules.

Background: Our current streaming telemetry aggregates at the request level and loses visibility into mid-stream tool invocations and structured outputs. This makes diagnosing regressions (e.g., a tool call causing intermittent latency spikes) difficult. We also need to ensure PII does not leak into observability when users stream raw content or tool outputs.

Acceptance criteria:
- Runtime emits a "segment" event for each logical output boundary (approx every N tokens or on tool/function call boundaries).
- Each segment contains metric fields: segment_id, sequence_index, latency_ms, token_count, bytes_out, model_variant, tool_call_count, error_flag.
- Segments are stamped with a trace/span id and parent request id; spans are linkable in Jaeger/OTel.
- Observability pipeline applies redaction rules to any free-text fields before persistent logging. Redaction succeeds with configurable sensitivity profiles.
- SDK compatibility layer provides a graceful fallback for pre-structured-output clients (keeps existing wire format while attaching side-channel segment metadata).
- Integration tests cover: tool-calling mid-stream (function calls), structured JSON output streaming, and trace/span integrity under high concurrency.

Design notes and decisions:
- "Segment" vs "chunk": we adopt "segment" for logical boundaries (token-count and semantic boundaries) to reduce confusion with transport-level "chunks". Each segment represents a semantically useful slice (e.g., until a tool call or sentence boundary).
- Span model: create a top-level Request span, then create Segment spans as children. Tool calls spawn sibling spans with a link to the segment that triggered them. This supports per-segment latency attribution and tool-level breakdowns.
- Redaction model: two-stage. 1) inline best-effort redaction at generation time using pattern matchers and a configurable allowlist/denylist. 2) post-ingest redaction in the observability pipeline for guaranteed removal before long-term storage. Both stages run with configurable sampling to limit CPU during high throughput.
- Storage and cardinality: metrics will be emitted to Prometheus-compatible aggregates (histograms/counters) per model_variant and route, with segment-level events sent to our event store for a rolling 7-day window. Full-text segment payloads are only stored when allowed by tenant settings (default: disabled).

Implementation plan:
1) Runtime: add SegmentEmitter that triggers on token thresholds, semantic boundaries, or tool-call events. Attach minimal metadata to reduce serialization overhead.
2) Tracing: instrument SegmentEmitter to start a child span and emit an OTLP span with attributes for segment_id, token_count, latency_ms.
3) Redaction: integrate existing redact-service library into the emission path with a fast-path for no-redaction tenants. Add configuration toggles (sensitivity profiles).
4) SDK compatibility: add Content-Metadata header (non-breaking) that delivers segment metadata for older SDKs via sidecar events; new SDKs will parse segment envelopes in-band.
5) Observability pipeline: update log forwarder to run post-ingest redaction, wire in segment->request join to allow reconstructing full streams in dashboards.
6) Tests & performance: microbenchmarks to measure 95th percentile latency increase (target <2ms added per segment under normal load). Add e2e tests simulating 10k concurrent streams.

Trade-offs considered:
- Inline redaction increases CPU on the hot path; mitigated by sampling and fast-match filters.
- Emitting segment-level events increases cardinality; mitigated by aggregation and a short retention window.
- Adding tracing spans per segment can increase trace volume; we will apply dynamic sampling and drop attributes for high-volume tenants.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): enable for internal tenants only, gather performance metrics and trace coverage.
- Phase 2 (opt-in): expose to customers behind a feature flag; update SDK beta to parse new side-channel metadata.
- Phase 3 (default-on for new routes): enable by default for newly created routes with clear opt-out for sensitive tenants.

Observability and dashboards:
- New dashboard: "Streamflow Segments" showing per-route segment rate, median segment latency, percent of segments triggering tool calls, and redaction hit rate.
- Link to existing traces: each segment has trace/span links visible in request timeline view.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Streamflow+Segmentation+Telemetry
- Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/942 (WIP)
- Prototype dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streamflow/segments

Open questions:
- How aggressive should inline redaction be for languages with ambiguous tokenization? Proposal: per-tenant language profiles and a default conservative setting.
- Sampling defaults: 1% trace sampling for high-volume tenants, 100% for internal and enterprise by contract.

Next steps:
- Finish runtime emitter implementation (Diego) and create canary build.
- Request security review for redaction profiles and PII handling (Maya).
- Add e2e scenarios covering tool-function calls that return structured JSON mid-stream.
